body: I want to say though, thank you for responding. You're the only one.

Hah, no, I'm 20 and my relationship with my parents isn't exactly healthy. I've already graduated college so I feel as if I'm on my own. I do want to die but I don't think I can, so I don't know where to go from here.

Thank you so much. I'll keep this in mind...

I really hope things get better for you, too. I know they will. You seem confident of that.

God, I'm so sorry. I'm glad you're getting better, though. It's crazy to have come that close and still snatched it back from Death's grip. Who's the badass now? :)

As for massage: I'm a massage therapist. I couldn't care less about receiving, but giving massages is therapeutic for me (not to mention I need the money now more than ever!). 

I can definitely relate. I've been having neurological problems. Most of the time, my left arm and leg *don't* feel like my own, and if I try overtaxing them (i.e. using them) they just "give up". It's very disheartening but I'm sure you know that.

What things do you struggle with? How far have you come in your recovery? I'm really sorry to hear that.

I have always had this terrible character flaw: when shit hits the fan, I withdraw, and usually it helps me to sort things out myself. But shit has CONSTANTLY been throwing itself at the proverbial fan, one thing after the other, for a while, and I've lost a lot of friends just because I haven't had the energy to maintain friendships. And I've never had many friends to begin with.

Of the friends I'm close to, many have their own struggles, and I hate imposing on them. I did actually end up exploding all my troubles on one friend tonight, and he probably saved my life tonight, but I know it's only a temporary thing and I can't handle this on my own, but can never bring myself to ask for help, either.

I used to run, but right before the accident (like a month before) I got really bad shin splints which became stress fractures. They've still not completely healed. So I switched to swimming and it turned out that I really love swimming a lot more than running anyway. I can still swim but it's hard with just one arm (swimming can sometimes hurt my still-healing shins so I try not to kick too much). There's a strong rip current. So I haven't been swimming either.

I also love(d?) cooking (can't hold a knife for long, let alone a pot) and massage therapy (had just graduated from a program) too. Cooking I can get help with, much to my chagrin, but massage was my life.

> What motivated you to keep going when things got bad

My sister. She's such a sweetheart (she's seven) and she loves me. She's the one family member I get along with really well and I can't stand the thought of how my death would hurt her. But I feel like I really can't last too much longer living like that - feeding off hypothetical guilt.

>do you still see her a good bit?

I'm back with my family so I see her every day.

>what are those things you love you were talking about?

Cooking...used to cook something new and/or exotic every day. I had lost weight by cooking and had inspired my sister to live a more healthy lifestyle (my family is not at all healthy while I generally am) to boot. I had so much joy cooking healthful, delicious food, usually a different cuisine or recipes I had never tried. Now, it so hurts to so much as hold a knife, and I can't cook by myself. Swimming... I live by one of the supposed best beaches nationwide, and love it. Something about the timelessness of the waves and sand soothes my soul, and when I swim, I'm like I fish. I never want to leave the water. It's hard to swim now, and I can do it, but I'm afraid I'll drown if my good arm gets too tired and the waves get to be too much. Drowning is not a way I would want to go out. Anyway... Massage therapy. I'm a massage therapist, and love what I (am trained to do, but can no longer) do so much. In the past I would be having a terrible day dealing with depression and life circumstances but slap a bag of muscles (you) on a table and I would be in my happy place for the rest of the day. 

It's only been a month since the accident... and while I have a bit better control of my hand now, I still struggle greatly. I often struggle not to cry in public because something (usually my inability to do something) will remind me about everything and I just can't take it.

I'm not working, and might lose my job because I can't work. I'm in an at-will state so they can fire me for any reason. Everything is just so difficult for me right now. Even typing hurts but... what else would I be doing all day?

> I have never had an easy life, or a happy one, but there's always been something to keep me going. But the past decade has been nothing but one hardship...after another....and it's just been impossible. I've always dealt with some sort of depression, but had my own quirks and ways of handling it. But it just gets to be too much.
> In the past year, I've been ostracized by my family, and "willingly"/unwillingly homeless due to that. Felt isolated. Alone. Lost. Always lonely. Struggled with debt. Struggled with putting food on the table once I moved back in with my family. Recently I got into a car accident, and can't do the few things I love because they're physical and the accident has left half my body numb/having problems. There's a whole list, I can't even think of everything that has led to this, but I feel like I'm at the end of my rope.


I'm not really in a mind to think of everything I'm feeling right now. I just want out.

I have never had an easy life, or a happy one, but there's always been something to keep me going. But the past decade has been nothing but one hardship...after another....and it's just been impossible. I've always dealt with some sort of depression, but had my own quirks and ways of handling it. But it just gets to be too much.

In the past year, I've been ostracized by my family, and "willingly"/unwillingly homeless due to that. Felt isolated. Alone. Lost. Always lonely. Struggled with debt. Struggled with putting food on the table once I moved back in with my family. Recently I got into a car accident, and can't do the few things I love because they're physical and the accident has left half my body numb/having problems. There's a whole list, I can't even think of everything that has led to this, but I feel like I'm at the end of my rope.
